brief: Goldman's prime book estimates roughly two-thirds of hedge funds down on Oct 22, as a momentum and crowded-longs factor unwind (Momentum -2.6 SD, Crowded Longs -2.8 SD, the worst daily factor sell-off since the week of Liberation Day, April 2025) hit funds across strategies. For the first time since COVID, all three broad equity HF strategies fell more than 1% the same day: Global Fundamental L/S -1.1% (beta-driven; -3.5% MTD, +9.1% YTD; Asia sub-book -1.7%/-8.8% MTD/+14.6% YTD, TMT sub-book -1.8%/-8.6% MTD/+9.0% YTD), Global Systematic L/S -1.2% (momentum and crowded longs the key drivers, +19.1% YTD), and Multi-Strats (4.5x leverage) -1.4% (momentum, info tech and crowded longs the largest detractors). The note forwards two prior updates from Oct 15, when the same momentum/crowding dynamic hit: at 10:30am momentum was down 3.4 SD and crowded shorts were squeezing +1.2 SD, which the note flagged would make it only the third day in 2026, after Feb 4 and Jul 28, that all three strategies fell more than 80bps together (never seen from COVID through 2025); by the close all three had indeed moved together again.
